decisions.reason: As a low-cost, complementary care product in a growing flooring business, it preserves option value while the firm learns demand and supports the installed base.
This maintenance oil is a close extension of the firm's core system offer, and its likely modest carrying cost makes continued market presence worthwhile until sales potential is clearer.
Although narrower and somewhat overlapping with other wood-floor care products, it still fits the firm's full-service positioning and is cheap enough to keep while uncertainty remains.
A moisture-protection underlay strengthens the flooring system offer and bundling potential, so the option to continue learning about uptake still outweighs its moderate carrying cost.
This underlay foam is more commodity-like and overlaps with other underlay options, but it remains adjacent to the core range and should be retained until its market value is better resolved.

The oak parquet floor is close to the firm's established core business, and despite higher carrying costs than accessories it is strategically important enough to keep while demand information accumulates.
